column1: # OnConflict{UpdateAll} upsert of a whole security-state row. Each row says why the site
# is acceptable, or that it is not (UNSAFE-OPEN #issue) and stays listed only so main
# stays green until the fix lands.
# Columns: file <TAB> function <TAB> model <TAB> reason <TAB> expires <TAB> added_by <TAB> reviewed_by
#   SAFE-CAS     a conditional write (WHERE on the state column) and no narrower writer of
#                any other column of that table exists, so nothing can be reverted.
#   RESIDUAL     a stale revert is possible, of the columns named, none of which gates
#   UNSAFE-OPEN  a real race; the issue tracks the fix. Not "accepted": remove the row
#   NO-CALLER    the primitive has no production caller; any new caller needs its own
#   FIXED-NO-CALLER  the race is fixed (every caller moved to a column-scoped write) and a
#                derived sweep asserts no production caller remains; the row stays only while
#                the full-row primitive itself still exists. Names the fixing test.
#   pending: #N  an open PR fixes this site; the row expires (expires column) and
#   arrives with #N  pre-registered for a site an open PR creates or renames; may match
#   Every reason starts with one of these classes and then says why
# reviewed_by must be non-empty and differ from added_by
# CALLER rows (model column "calls:<LocalStorage method>") belong to
# one row per (file, enclosing function, writer method it calls). The caller is the
# stale writer when it hands the primitive a struct it read earlier. Classification of a
# caller row is the callee row's class plus whether THIS caller's read/write is gated.
# Rows marked "[carried #2725]" restate the independently reviewed verdict of the same
# caller in #2725's ledger (reviewed_by C-GUARD3-EXEMPT-REVIEW); rows marked
# "[callee verdict]" had no #2725 row (or the function was renamed/split since) and restate
# the reviewed verdict of the callee row above, with added_by SMALL-FIX-1: they still need

column4: SAFE-CAS: conditional on state='open' (WHERE id AND state); the only transition is open->closed by CloseAccessReviewCampaign, a losing racer matches 0 rows, and no other writer changes any column of an open campaign (purge deletes only closed ones). STORE-STALE-NOV-2: cannot revert a close; open->closed is one-way and purge only deletes closed rows (TestFullRowWriters_NarrowWriteSurvivesStaleTransition_UpdateAccessReviewCampaign).

SAFE-CAS: conditional on decision='pending' and an open campaign; on main no other writer changes an item row, and the snapshot columns are immutable. STORE-STALE-NOV-2: cannot revert a decision; pending->decided is one-way and the item has no other writer (TestFullRowWriters_NarrowWriteSurvivesStaleTransition_UpdateAccessReviewItem).

SAFE-CAS: conditional on state='pending'; no other writer changes a pending request's columns (purge removes only resolved rows). STORE-STALE-NOV-2: cannot revert a reject or the secret-delete close; every other writer moves the row off pending for good (closeApprovedSecretAccessRequests: approved->expired) and purge deletes (TestFullRowWriters_SecretDeleteCloseSurvivesStaleApprove_UpdateAccessRequest).

SAFE-CAS: conditional on state='pending'; every invitation writer goes through this transition, no column-narrower writer exists. STORE-STALE-NOV-2: cannot revert a revoke or accept; pending->terminal is one-way (resend writes the setup token, not this row) (TestFullRowWriters_NarrowWriteSurvivesStaleTransition_UpdateProjectInvitation).

SAFE-CAS: conditional on state=from; transitionMachineInTx re-reads under LockMachineIdentityForUpdate in the same tx, ClassifyMachineIdentity's UPDATE blocks on that row lock and then fails its state CAS. The only other writers are the project-delete cascade and its restore (column-scoped, both change state, so a stale classify loses the CAS; after a suspend+restore A->B->A it only adds its label, the cascade marker stays cleared). Worst case: one of two concurrent classifies is lost. STORE-STALE-NOV-2: cannot revert a revoke, suspend or cascade (TestFullRowWriters_CascadeSuspendSurvivesStaleClassify_TransitionMachineIdentityState, ..._CascadeSuspendAndRestoreThenStaleClassify_...). STORE-STALE-NOV-3: the one A->B->A on this table (cascade suspend, restore, admin suspend) lets a stale classify match and put the cleared cascade marker back; it stays inert, since a restore also needs the marker to equal the project's current deleted_at and updated_at to equal the marker, and the classify stamps its own updated_at (TestFullRowWriters_StaleClassifyAfterRestoreAndAdminSuspend_MarkerStaysInert_TransitionMachineIdentityState).

SAFE-CAS: conditional on state; every membership writer goes through this transition and changes only state-related columns. (The role-grant side effect of a racing activate/revoke is #2657/#2659, not a column revert.) STORE-STALE-NOV-2: cannot revert a revoke; no other writer of project_memberships exists and both callers re-read under the membership named lock (TestFullRowWriters_NarrowWriteSurvivesStaleTransition_TransitionProjectMembershipState).

SAFE-CAS: conditional on revoked=false AND approved=false; the only other writer (RevokeRiskExceptionIfNotRevoked) is column-scoped and makes this CAS miss. STORE-STALE-NOV-3: cannot revert a revoke; revoked and approved are both one-way and no other writer changes any column of the row (TestFullRowWriters_NarrowWriteSurvivesStaleTransition_ApproveRiskExceptionIfPending).
